by: pkg:VERIFY (4 dtype_significant controls added 2026-11-11 in the repair step, review MF5; 2 identity-key controls added 2026-11-11, Amendment 3; 4 row-identity controls added 2026-11-11, lead ruling LR1.4; 2 LR16 controls added 2026-11-12, lead ruling LR16)
note: expectations written from FULL_PREREG sections 3 and 9 before any run

controls.name: dt_text_frame
controls.why: text columns are object on 2.3.3 and str on 3.x; values equal; unflagged -> DTYPE_ONLY

controls.name: dt_groupby_sum
controls.why: group keys end up in an object (2.3.3) or str (3.x) index; sums equal

controls.name: dt_datetime_frame
controls.why: parsed dates are datetime64[ns] on 2.3.3 and a coarser unit on 3.x; canonical timestamps equal

controls.name: dt_column_labels
controls.why: result is the Index of column labels: object on 2.3.3, str on 3.x; labels equal

controls.name: dt_value_counts_series
controls.why: distinct counts, so order is fixed; only the index dtype differs

controls.name: dt_pivot_table
controls.why: row and column labels are text; dtype of the label indexes differs, values equal

controls.name: dt_to_dict_keys
controls.why: a plain dict of Python strings and floats cannot differ by dtype: IDENTICAL (guards against calling every program DTYPE_ONLY)

controls.name: ord_dataframe_value_counts
controls.why: DataFrame.value_counts(sort=False) lists groups sorted on 2.3.3 and in first-appearance order on 3.x; unflagged -> ORDER_ONLY

controls.name: ord_dataframe_value_counts_frame
controls.why: the same as a DataFrame with a default index (index ignored by the oracle)

controls.name: ord_concat_dates
controls.why: concat(axis=1, sort=False) of date-indexed frames: index sorted on 2.3.3, first appearance on 3.x

controls.name: ord_and_dtype_unflagged
controls.why: order and index dtype both change; unflagged -> not drift (ORDER_ONLY; DTYPE_ONLY would also be non-drift)

controls.name: tie_stable_sorted_counts_series
controls.why: sorted by count; every group has count 2, so the order differs only among ties of the key

controls.name: tie_stable_sorted_counts_frame
controls.why: same, as a DataFrame with key column n

controls.name: tie_partial_ties_frame
controls.why: one group has count 3, four have count 2, one has count 1: after a stable descending sort the count column is equal at every row, only the cities inside the count-2 block change places

controls.name: pos_order_beyond_ties_index
controls.why: flagged on the (distinct) group labels: any reordering is beyond ties

controls.name: pos_order_beyond_ties_frame
controls.why: flagged on city; the same frame lists the groups in a different order, cities all distinct per row

controls.name: pos_order_beyond_ties_partial_key
controls.why: same data as tie_partial_ties_frame but the frame is not sorted by n: the n column itself changes order (3,2,2,2,2,1 vs 2,2,2,2,1,3), so the change is beyond ties of the key

controls.name: pos_order_concat_dates
controls.why: date index in a different order, flagged on the index

controls.name: pos_dtype_text_frame
controls.why: dtype_significant card, text columns change dtype (object -> str)

controls.name: pos_dtype_datetime_frame
controls.why: dtype_significant card, datetime unit changes

controls.name: flag_dtype_on_order_only
controls.why: dtype_significant card on a program whose result changes order and index dtype: both ORDER_ONLY and DTYPE_DRIFT are defensible readings; recorded, not scored

controls.name: dtsig_float_frame_text_labels
controls.why: dtype_significant card; float cells are float64 on both sides, only the text row index and the column-label Index change object -> str: not DTYPE_DRIFT

controls.name: dtsig_series_date_index
controls.why: dtype_significant card; integer values unchanged, only the unit of the parsed date index changes: not DTYPE_DRIFT

controls.name: dtsig_value_counts_series
controls.why: dtype_significant card; distinct counts (int64 on both sides), only the dtype of the text index changes: not DTYPE_DRIFT

controls.name: dtsig_index_result
controls.why: dtype_significant card; the result is an Index of text labels, so its dtype is the dtype of its values (object -> str): DTYPE_DRIFT

controls.name: idkey_same_order_groupby
controls.why: order_significant with the identity key __index__; groupby sorts its text keys on every version, so the index label at every row position is the same; only the label and text dtypes change: not ORDER_DRIFT

controls.name: idkey_same_order_file_rows
controls.why: order_significant with the identity key __index__ on a file-order result (default row labels 0..n-1 kept in file order on every version); text columns change dtype only: not ORDER_DRIFT

controls.name: lr1_idkey_column_default_index_frame
controls.why: LR1.4 must be ORDER_DRIFT (table form): identity key __index__, the key (city) held as a column, default index 0..n-1, rows reordered beyond ties (cities distinct); LR1.2 uses the whole row as the key

controls.name: lr1_idkey_column_default_index_list
controls.why: LR1.4 must be ORDER_DRIFT (list form): the same rows as a Python list of (city, n) tuples, reordered beyond ties; LR1.2 uses the element at each position

controls.name: lr1_idkey_series_default_index
controls.why: Series form (LR1.2, review RV-2(c); added next to the two LR1.4 forms): the counts as a Series with a default index, values reordered beyond ties (3 moves from first to last); the whole row is the key

controls.name: lr1_namedkey_index_ties_only
controls.why: LR1.4 must be ORDER_ONLY: named key n held in the index (not a column), rows permuted among ties only (stable descending sort by n; only the cities inside the count-2 block change places); LR1.1 finds n among the index level names

controls.name: lr16_nonunique_index_ties_label
controls.why: LR16 (a) case: identity key __index__ on a non-unique index (plan; two rows per plan after a stable sort by plan); only rows that share a plan label change places, so under LR1 (key = index labels) the order differs only in ties: ORDER_ONLY; under the LR16 (a) sensitivity (whole row as key) ORDER_DRIFT

controls.name: lr16_key_not_found_reordered
controls.why: LR16 (b) case: named sort key total is neither a column nor an index level name of the result; rows reordered: under LR1 HRUN H1 ("sort key not found") ORDER_DRIFT; under the LR16 (b) sensitivity ORDER_ONLY

controls.name: num_identical_float
controls.why: same value

controls.name: num_below_relative_tol
controls.why: relative difference 1e-12 < 1e-11

controls.name: num_below_absolute_tol
controls.why: one zero but absolute difference 1e-12 < 1e-9: equal by the oracle tolerance

controls.name: num_small_scalar
controls.why: relative difference 1e-8 < 1e-6

controls.name: num_small_just_under
controls.why: relative difference 5e-7 < 1e-6

controls.name: num_substantive_just_over
controls.why: relative difference 2e-6 >= 1e-6

controls.name: num_substantive_scalar
controls.why: relative difference 1e-4

controls.name: num_zero_vs_nonzero
controls.why: exactly one of a, b is 0 -> relative difference 1 -> SUBSTANTIVE (absolute 1e-7 > 1e-9, so it is drift)

controls.name: num_sign_flip_tiny
controls.why: relative difference 2 (opposite signs), absolute 2e-8 > 1e-9

controls.name: num_integer_off_by_one
controls.why: integers are compared exactly

controls.name: num_text_differs
controls.why: text compared exactly

controls.name: num_frame_all_small
controls.why: same shape and labels, every differing cell numeric and below 1e-6 relative

controls.name: num_frame_one_large_cell
controls.why: one cell differs by 1%: SUBSTANTIVE although another cell differs by 1e-8

controls.name: num_frame_extra_row
controls.why: shape differs

controls.name: num_frame_label_differs
controls.why: column label differs

controls.name: num_null_pattern
controls.why: null pattern differs

controls.name: num_null_kinds_equal
controls.why: None, NaN and pd.NA are all null (section 3): no value difference

controls.name: num_bool_vs_int
controls.why: booleans treated as 0/1: dtype difference only

controls.name: num_no_result_on_target
controls.why: the 3.x run completes without defining result: drift (NO_RESULT, section 3)

controls.name: loud_raise_on_target
controls.why: the 3.x run raises: LOUD, never drift
